source.title: 诊断学（第10版）
source.section: 第五篇 辅助检查 第一章 心电图 第六节

textbook_summary: Ventricular flutter lacks normal QRS-T complexes and shows continuous rapid, relatively regular, large-amplitude oscillations at 200-250/min.
Ventricular fibrillation lacks identifiable QRS-T complexes and shows highly irregular oscillations of varying amplitude at 200-500/min.
Ventricular flutter/fibrillation do not provide effective cardiac output.
limitations: A single projected-source teaching morphology, not anatomical localization or a realistic multifocal electrical model.
Ventricular flutter uses a C1-continuous sinusoid-like polynomial. The VF table repeats every 16.384 s without automatic coarse/fine evolution.
No normal P/QRS/T, normal atrial mechanics or effective ventricular ejection. This does not classify the electrical activity as asystole.
RC pressure decay is retained. Respiration/CO2 remain independent, without circulatory gas-exchange feedback or automatic apnea.
No new detector, alarm, defibrillation or resuscitation decision logic.
